listenings.text: Good morning, this is the beach report for Monday. The water temperature is eighteen degrees, so you still want a wetsuit. The swell comes from the south and it drops through the afternoon. High tide is at ten past seven, and the best spot at that time is the north end, near the rocks. The lifeguard tower opens at seven and it closes at five. One warning: the wind picks up after midday and it makes the water messy. Get in early.

My name is Emma and I live ten minutes from the beach. On school days I get up at half past five. I never eat before I surf, but I always drink water. My brother comes with me and he carries the gear, because he loses every argument. We paddle out at six and we stay for one hour. Then I go home, I have a shower, and I catch the bus at half past seven. My friends think I am crazy. I think they sleep too much.

reading.rtitle: A Monday at the surf academy
paras: Dave is a coach at a surf academy on the Australian coast. His week starts at five in the morning. He checks the forecast on his phone before he gets up. If the swell is good, he sends one message to the group: see you at six.

At six the students arrive. They take their gear from the van and they put on their wetsuits. Dave never starts a session without a briefing. He explains the tide, he points at the best spot, and he shows the students where the lifeguard sits.
The first hour is hard. Beginners paddle a lot and catch nothing. They wipe out, they laugh, they try again. Dave doesn't shout. He watches from the water and he corrects one thing at a time.
The session finishes at eight and the students go to school. Dave stays. He surfs alone for another hour, every single Monday.
